account:
ALL OBSERVATIONS (hand enumeration, no code; valid only within stated bounds; non-occurrences prove nothing beyond them). Bounds: Method 1 sweep 1≤a≤b≤c≤20, d≥c, d≤100; Method 2 BFS from (1,1,1,1), discard d>100.

PROCEDURE (reproducible). Method 1: for each sorted triple set M=4abc, P=a²+b²+c²; d must be the major root of t²−Mt+P=0, so (i) d|P, (ii) d+d′=M with dd′=P, (iii) non-root d>2abc (proved L1, answer:work:003-struct-core-v2); with d≤100 only abc≤49 triples can hit, leaving a=1 (bc≤49), a=2 (bc≤24), a=3 (b=3,c≤5; b=c=4); test each divisor d of P with d>2abc for d+P/d=M. Method 2: mutate all four coordinates, re-sort, keep d≤100.

(a) VERIFIED TABLE (OBS, d≤100), one-line checks:
v0=(1,1,1,1): 4=4·1.
v1=(1,1,1,3): 1+1+1+9=12=4·3.
v2=(1,1,3,11): 1+1+9+121=132=4·33.
v3=(1,1,11,41): 1+1+121+1681=1804=4·451.
Out-of-bound hit retained for honesty (c≤20): (1,3,11,131): 1+9+121+17161=17292=4·4323, d=131>100.
Nothing else: e.g. a=1,b=2 requires d|c²+5 and d+d′=8c; every c=2..20 fails (closest c=7: 54+1=55≠56); a=1,b=1,c∉{1,3,11} fails likewise (c=7: 51+1=52≠28, etc.); all a≥2 candidates die since no divisor of P exceeds 2abc. Method-2 BFS: v0→v1 (4−1=3); v1: mutate 1→11=v2, mutate 3→1=v0; v2: mutate 3→41=v3, mutate 1→131 (discard), mutate 11→1=v1; v3: mutate 11→153, mutate 1→1803 (both discarded), mutate 41→3=v2. BFS vertex set {v0,v1,v2,v3}.

(b) c=d within bound: NONE (OBS); only the root has c=d, consistent with proved L2.

(c) Two height-decreasing mutations or two parents: NONE (OBS). Mutation spectra: v1: {11>3, 1<3}; v2: {131>11, 41>11, 1<11}; v3: {1803>41, 153>41, 3<41} — exactly one d-lowering mutation each (at the maximum), consistent with proved D2/D3.

(d) Methods 1 and 2 AGREE EXACTLY within d≤100 (OBS): identical vertex sets; no Method-1 solution unreachable from the root, so no local refutation of D1. The d=131 hit is v2's BFS child, so agreement persists through d≤131.

(e) Parent edges (OBS): d′=4abc−d: v1: 4−3=1; v2: 12−11=1; v3: 44−41=3; each 1≤d′<d, edges v1→v0, v2→v1, v3→v2.

(f) Induction failure modes: NONE within bound (OBS). Re-sorting after a d-mutation produced no tie and no equal-height parent; equal-coordinate subtlety (v2 has a=b, mutating a vs b coincide) occurs only on the height-increasing side, as proved. Recurring near-misses d+d′=P+1≠M (e.g. a=1,b=2,c=7: 55 vs 56) explain the sparsity of hits but are not solutions.

Depth/height (OBS): depths 0,1,2,3 at d=1,3,11,41; N(1)=1, N(3)=2, N(11)=3, N(100)=4.
assumptions: The abc≤49 pruning of the Method-1 sweep uses the already-proved descent lemma L1 (d′<d at non-root vertices, answer:work:003-struct-core-v2); the d|P and d+d′=4abc prunes follow from the quadratic alone.
All arithmetic was done by hand; no code was executed, per constraint C2.

claims.statement: OBSERVATION (d≤100, sweep 1≤a≤b≤c≤20): the complete set of solutions with d≤100 is {(1,1,1,1),(1,1,1,3),(1,1,3,11),(1,1,11,41)}, each verified by direct substitution (4=4·1; 12=4·3; 132=4·33; 1804=4·451).

OBSERVATION (d≤100): Method 1 (direct divisor search) and Method 2 (BFS from the root) yield exactly the same vertex set; no direct-search solution is unreachable from (1,1,1,1), so no local refutation of D1; agreement persists through d≤131 since (1,3,11,131) is a BFS child of (1,1,3,11).

OBSERVATION (d≤100): no non-root vertex has c=d, and every non-root vertex has exactly one height-decreasing mutation (at the maximum coordinate d); no vertex has two parents. Consistent with proved L2/D2/D3; non-occurrence within the bound proves nothing beyond it.

OBSERVATION (parent edges): for v1,v2,v3, d′=4abc−d equals 1,1,3 respectively, each 1≤d′<d, giving the chain v3→v2→v1→root; depths 0,1,2,3 occur at heights 1,3,11,41; N(1)=1, N(3)=2, N(11)=3, N(100)=4.

OBSERVATION (d≤100): no induction failure modes — re-sorting after d-mutation produced no ties or equal-height parents; the equal-coordinate mutation coincidence at (1,1,3,11) (a=b) stays on the height-increasing side; near-misses d+d′=P+1≠4abc (e.g. a=1,b=2,c=7: 55≠56) are not solutions.
INFERENCE: the tree is not a path — (1,1,3,11) has two children, (1,1,11,41) and (1,3,11,131) — so branching begins at depth 2 and N(H) counts a genuinely branching tree.

counterevidence: Hand enumeration without code risks arithmetic slips; mitigated by two independent methods agreeing exactly and by one-line substitution checks for every listed vertex.
All non-occurrence statements (no c=d, no multiple parents, no cycles) hold only within d≤100 and prove nothing beyond the bound.
The abc≤49 prune depends on proved L1; if L1 were wrong the Method-1 sweep would be incomplete — but L1 is proved in answer:work:003-struct-core-v2.
